args.title: gRPC migration verified at commit 453aa7f (26/26 tests pass)
args.body:
Continuation verification of the site-readings gRPC migration at HEAD 453aa7f.

Inspected proto/energy.proto, service/wire.js, service/grpc_server.js, service/grpc_client.js, test/server.test.js, test/integration.test.js, README.md, and confirmed test/rest.test.js is unchanged from the REST baseline (not weakened or deleted).

Ran the suite in-process: `node --test --test-isolation=none` -> 26 tests, 26 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped (~310 ms). The literal default `node --test` fails in this sandbox with spawn EPERM while the runner tries to spawn isolated worker processes; this is the documented fallback case in README, not a product test failure.

Coverage observed by running it: real gRPC client-to-server GetReading and StreamReadings; values compared with the REST console for every fixture site; source order and limit semantics for absent/0/3/99 limits; unknown site -> NOT_FOUND/unknown_site (never an empty result); negative limit -> INVALID_ARGUMENT/invalid_limit; exact epoch-millisecond atMs; one sub-16KiB gRPC frame per Reading; malformed protobuf, oversized request and unknown-method status mapping; 20 concurrent unary calls.

Git working tree clean; all migration and test files are tracked at 453aa7f. No code change was required in this continuation: the formal attempt was opened at a basis commit that already contained the committed migration, so its world has no delta and must not be re-run blindly.

I re-read the implementation and tests rather than trusting the prior commit message, then ran the real suite in-process: `node --test --test-isolation=none` -> 26 tests, 26 pass, 0 fail (324 ms). The literal `node --test` cannot start isolated worker processes in this sandbox (spawn EPERM), which is the documented fallback case in README; it is not a test failure. The run exercises real HTTP/2 client-to-server unary and streaming calls, REST-vs-gRPC value/ordering/limit equivalence, unknown-site NOT_FOUND/unknown_site, negative-limit INVALID_ARGUMENT/invalid_limit, exact epoch-ms atMs, one sub-16KiB frame per Reading, malformed/oversized/unknown-method status mapping, and concurrency. test/rest.test.js is unchanged from the baseline. The formal grpc-contract attempt was based on the same commit and had no delta; it was closed as a successor and the redundant task graph was retired in revision 1 rather than re-running or fabricating a result. The deliverable is ready for operator review and promotion; this conclusion is not acceptance.

args.title: gRPC migration verified at commit 453aa7f (26/26 tests pass)
args.body:
Continuation verification of the site-readings gRPC migration at HEAD 453aa7f.

Inspected proto/energy.proto, service/wire.js, service/grpc_server.js, service/grpc_client.js, test/server.test.js, test/integration.test.js, README.md, and confirmed test/rest.test.js is unchanged from the REST baseline (not weakened or deleted).

Ran the suite in-process: `node --test --test-isolation=none` -> 26 tests, 26 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped (~310 ms). The literal default `node --test` fails in this sandbox with spawn EPERM while the runner tries to spawn isolated worker processes; this is the documented fallback case in README, not a product test failure.

Coverage observed by running it: real gRPC client-to-server GetReading and StreamReadings; values compared with the REST console for every fixture site; source order and limit semantics for absent/0/3/99 limits; unknown site -> NOT_FOUND/unknown_site (never an empty result); negative limit -> INVALID_ARGUMENT/invalid_limit; exact epoch-millisecond atMs; one sub-16KiB gRPC frame per Reading; malformed protobuf, oversized request and unknown-method status mapping; 20 concurrent unary calls.

Git working tree clean; all migration and test files are tracked at 453aa7f. No code change was required in this continuation: the formal attempt was opened at a basis commit that already contained the committed migration, so its world has no delta and must not be re-run blindly.
